How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as
noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read. Your comments must be received by 5:00
P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, May 21, 2024

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Harrington

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 21, 2024  2
   B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – APRIL 2024

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2023-2024 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 23-36) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2023-24 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for April 2024.

  D. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH WILLIAM HEZMALHALCH
  ARCHITECTS (WHA) FOR ARCHITECTURAL, URBAN DESIGN, AND
  HISTORIC PRESERVATION PROFESSIONAL SERVICES

  On January 4, 2021, the City issued a Request for Proposals (RFP 21-01) for a
  qualified firm to provide architectural, urban design, and historic preservation
  professional services. The City selected William Hezmalhalch Architects (WHA)
  as the firm that best met the criteria outlined in the Request for Proposal. WHA
  has met the performance expectations as outlined in the Scope of Work. Staff
  recommends a fee at a not-to-exceed amount of $40,000 yearly for a three-
  year period, inclusive of all costs and services through June 1, 2027. Funds have

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 21, 2024  3
   been included in both the current year and proposed 2024-2025 Fiscal Year
  budgets.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Professional Services
  Agreement with William Hezmalhalch Architects and authorize the City
  Manager to execute said agreement and issue purchase order in the amount of
  $40,000.

  E. AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL AND RELATED
  COMPANIES (DEVELOPER), RELATED TO A REIMBURSEMENT PROGRAM
  FOR THE PERMANENT LOCAL HOUSING ALLOCATION (PLHA) FUNDING
  FOR THE 405 S. DEL MAR PROJECT

  The Los Angeles County Development Authority (LACDA), on behalf of Los
  Angeles County and its participating cities, has applied for funding for the grant
  program known as the Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) Program
  from the California Department of Housing & Community Development. The
  allocation is based on real estate recording fees, and the City of San Gabriel will
  be allocated $982,382 over a four-year period from the grant. The City of San
  Gabriel has the opportunity to utilize this funding opportunity toward eligible
  housing activities as identified in the PLHA grant guidelines. As such, staff will
  be utilizing the $982,382 toward the affordable housing project at 405 S. Del
  Mar Avenue. In order to facilitate a reimbursement program between the PLHA
  grant funds and services rendered by the Related Companies, an agreement
  between the City of San Gabriel and Related Companies (Developer) is
  necessary. The City is expected to have access to the $982,382 PLHA
  reimbursable grant funds through LACDA. The City has already allocated
  $480,191 from the PLHA fund, which must be expended by December 31, 2024.
  The Year 3 funding of $334,526 must be spent by December 2025. By December
  2026, $167,665 of the PLHA grant funds must be expended.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 21, 2024  4
   Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  an agreement between Related Companies, and the City of San Gabriel for the
  grant agreement.

  F. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 24-22, RELATED TO PERMANENT LOCAL
  HOUSING ALLOCATION (PLHA) YEAR 4 FUNDING AND PROPOSED
  ELIGIBLE ACTIVITIES

  The Los Angeles County Development Authority (LACDA), on behalf of Los
  Angeles County and its participating cities, will be applying for funding for Year
  Four of the Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) Program from the
  California Department of Housing & Community Development. The allocation
  is based on real estate recording fees, and it is estimated that the City of San
  Gabriel will be allocated $167,665 from the $9 million grant for the period of
  July 1, 2024 – June 30, 2025 (Year Four). The City of San Gabriel has the
  opportunity to utilize the this funding for the eligible housing activities as
  identified in the PLHA grant guidelines.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-22, which
  approves the following actions:

  1. Elect the following eligible activities, subject to the State approval, for Year
  Four of the 5-Year Permanent Local Housing Allocation grant period:
  (1) The predevelopment, development, acquisition, rehabilitation, and
  preservation of multifamily, residential live-work, rental housing that is
  affordable to extremely low-, very low-, or moderate-income
  households, including necessary operating subsidies.

  2. Allocate, upon State approval, $167,665 of the Year Four Permanent Local
  Housing Allocation allocation toward eligible activity #1, and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute new contracts (and any other
  required documents) with Los Angeles County Development Authority for
  the 5-year Permanent Local Housing Allocation Plan grant period and for
  year Four of the allocation and make adjustments as necessary to reflect the
  actual allocation of funds to San Gabriel.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 21, 2024  5
   G. PURCHASE OF PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS REPORTING SOFTWARE

  The Police Department seeks to implement a comprehensive case management
  software with a forward-facing portal that will assist in documenting,
  referencing, and storing events such as use of force, pursuits, and complaints.
  Additionally, the system will provide management with early intervention
  opportunities to address training and behavioral issues. The Fiscal Year 2023-
  2024 adopted budget for Contractual Services-General, 121-751-00-22-000,
  included $25,000 to pay for software no longer in use. The savings from
  terminating this contract can be reallocated to this project, which has an initial
  cost of $14,500. Once purchased, the annual licensing fee for continued use will
  be $9,600.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into an agreement with Versaterm, a global public safety software company, for
  the product IA Pro software.

  H. ALL CITY MANAGEMENT SERVICES CONTRACT RENEWAL FOR CROSSING
  GUARD SERVICES FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $187,545

  The City has had a Professional Services Agreement with All City Management
  Services (ACMS), Incorporated to provide school crossing guard services since
  2014. The current contract expires on June 30, 2024. Crossing guard services
  are currently budgeted in the Police Department’s Contractual Services #121-
  751-00-22-000 in the amount of $200,000 for FY 2024-25. The fiscal impact for
  Fiscal Year 2024-2025 would be $187,545, an increase of $13,881. The new rates
  reflect the Los Angeles County price increases due to inflation.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into a one-year agreement Professional Services Agreement with All City
  Management Services for crossing guard services for an annual amount of not

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 21, 2024  6
   to exceed $187,545 and then reevaluate their services and other opportunities
  for services in Fiscal Year 2024-25.

  I. ORDINANCE NO. 707 DELETING TITLE III, CHAPTER 33.50-33.57 FROM
  THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE TO DISSOLVE THE HUMAN EQUITY,
  ACCESS AND RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION – SECOND READING AND
  ADOPTION

  Adoption of Ordinance No. 707 would dissolve the Human Equity, Access and
  Relations (HEAR) Commission. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive full reading and adopt Ordinance
  No. 707 entitled, An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel,
  California, Deleting Title III, Chapter 33, Sections 33.50-33.57 of the San Gabriel
  Municipal Code to Remove the Human Equity, Access and Relations
  Commission.

  J. COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION 2024 ANNUAL WORKPLAN

  The Annual Workplan is intended to guide the work of the Community Services
  Commission and outline the areas of focus for the Fiscal Year 2024-25. It
  includes proposed programs and projects that will be implemented and
  completed throughout the year and into 2025. The Commissioners had an open
  and constructive dialogue to develop a plan that best fits in alignment with the
  purpose and scope of the Community Services Commission as well as the City
  of San Gabriel’s Mission. There is no anticipated fiscal impact related to this
  item. Should funds be needed to complete any of the projects listed that cannot
  be absorbed into the existing departmental budget, a separate funding request
  will be made to the City Council at that time.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and approve the FY 2024-2025
  Community Services Commission’s Annual Workplan.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 21, 2024  7
  5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. REQUEST FROM THE FAMILY OF LATE CHIEF ERNIE SALAS TO PLACE A
  PLAQUE IN HIS HONOR IN PLAZA PARK

  In April 2021, the Native Sons of the Golden West gifted a plaque in honor of
  the late Chief Ernie Perez Teutimez to his family. His son, Andy Salas, has been
  in communication with City staff and would like to donate his plaque to the City
  to be installed. This request was initially reviewed by the Historic Preservation
  and Cultural Resources Commission (HPCRC), which approved the placement.
  Since that time, additional information has been presented. The cost of
  installation is negligible and will be absorbed by the Public Works Department.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and discuss the following
  options:

  Option 1: Direct staff to place the plaque in the proposed location in Plaza Park.

  Option 2: As mentioned during the discussion about the west end of Smith
  Park, direct staff to propose a monument to be placed in Smith Park
  denoting the area as open/passive park space to pay tribute to all of
  the ancestors of the Gabrieleño tribe.

  Option 3: Take no action at this time.

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  Mayor Wu called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:42 P.M.

  San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Harrington

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Vice Mayor
  Menchaca, and Mayor John Wu.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,

I  Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark. Public Works Director/City
  Engineer Greg de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace,
  Finance  Director  William  Kaholokula,  Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Community Development Director Aldo Cervantes,
  Police Chief Edward Elizalde, and Assistant City Clerk
  Marilyn Bonus.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  A. THREAT TO PUBLIC FACILITIES (GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 54957[a])

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and

I  request meeting agendas.

  Staff requested that Item 11 A be removed from the agenda. A motion was made by

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. REQUEST FROM THE FAMILY OF LATE CHIEF ERNIE SALAS TO PLACE A
  PLAQUE IN HIS HONOR IN PLAZA PARK

  Mary Cammarano, resident, in regard to Option 1, questioned if the Mission Church
  had been consulted.

  The following spoke or provided comments objecting to the placement of the
  plaque as written: Anthony Morales, Tribal Chief and Chairman of the Gabrielino
  San Gabriel Band of Mission Indians, resident; and Mary Garcia, President, Native
  Sons of the Golden West/Ramona Parlor.

  The following spoke or provided comments in favor of Option 1: Victoria Jones; Dr.

I  Christina Swindall, Secretary of Gabrielino Band of Mission Indians - Kizh Nation;
  Elizabeth Silva; Andy Salas, resident, on behalf of Tribal Government; Melissa
  Arechiga; Joe Castillo, past Grand President, Native Sons of the Golden West;
  Nadine Salas, Vice-Chair of Kizh-Gabrielino Band of Mission Indians; Jose Herrera,
  resident; Nicole Kristine Caamano, resident; Ray Adams, resident; Catherine Eredia,
  El Monte Historical Society; Mr. Hoffman; and Vincent Chente Montalvo.

  Joey Claro, representing the local chapter of Native Sons of the Golden West,
  stated that the local chapter takes no responsibility for this particular plaque.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 6  May 21 , 2024
   Discussion included that the plaque is a biography of a man, not a history of a
  tribe; the City's control of Plaza Park; the Archdiocese not being present to
  comment; inclusivity of indigenous groups; location of the plaque and future
  monument in Smith Park or Plaza Park; and preference of the Salas family for the
  plaque to be in Plaza Park.

  A motion was made by Council Member Ding, seconded by Council Member
  Harrington, to:
  1. Direct staff to place the plaque in the proposed location in Plaza Park.

I  2. Direct staff to propose a monument to be placed in Plaza Park denoting
  the area as open/passive park space to pay tribute to all of the ancestors of
  the Gabrieleno tribe.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HARRINGTON, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT
